channel.title: Four of Hearts Interactive News
channel.description: Company and game news from Four of Hearts Interactive.

item.title: Modern art has been informed about gravity.
item.description: Sling Nouveau begins with a pleasingly unreasonable idea: what if a sculptural playground also invited you to knock things down?

item.title: The rematch should not require technical support.
item.description: The website table has a deliberately simple brief: one fixed deal, as many attempts as you like.

item.title: Five cards. Plenty of opinions.
item.description: Euchre already provides enough uncertainty through the cards. The interface does not need to contribute.

item.title: Friendship, with penalty points.
item.description: Hearts has a lovely ability to make an innocent-looking card feel like a personal statement.

item.title: Confidence is not a bidding strategy. Apparently.
item.description: Spades deserves a table that respects the partnership.

item.title: One more deal. Entirely your own idea.
item.description: Solitaire should feel pleasantly inevitable: see the move, move the card, enjoy the little moment when everything starts to line up.

item.title: Let the cards cause the trouble.
item.description: War does not need a complicated introduction. It needs a dependable entrance, a clear table, and a satisfying flip.

item.title: A dragon is not a chore-management app.
item.description: A dragon should make you want to take off.

item.title: Your thumb has declined additional paperwork.
item.description: Thumb Command has a very clear staffing arrangement: one thumb, quite a lot of responsibility.

item.title: A dinosaur needs room to make an entrance.
item.description: Bobby’s world should feel lively before the first enemy arrives.

item.title: We would like the towers to be a little less normal.
item.description: The blade tower has set an inconveniently entertaining standard.

item.title: A city, not a directory of buttons.
item.description: BooYang City should invite you to look around and choose somewhere to go.

item.title: The planning department has rejected beige.
item.description: Funky Town needs room to be itself.

item.title: Shorter name. Unreasonably enthusiastic explosions.
item.description: The name going forward is Unicorn Blast.

item.title: The shoes have been asked to remain on the feet.
item.description: A beautiful dress-up game depends on details that cannot be negotiated away: fit, scale, layering, and characters who feel alive.

item.title: We have not established a maximum number of flowers.
item.description: Unicorn Land Adventures has its own creative brief: unicorns to personalize, habitats to shape, details to discover, and room to make something wonderfully yours.

item.title: Less spreadsheet. More bedside manner.
item.description: The Amigo is the point.

item.title: Your next counteroffer deserves better than “Um.”
item.description: SOVINTO is built around an understandable ambition: help people prepare for conversations that matter.

item.title: Twenty open tabs is not a research strategy.
item.description: Whomly’s direction is to turn scattered public professional information into useful context.

item.title: A table with room to think.
item.description: Gin Rummy is a two-player game. The interface should leave room for the decisions.

item.title: Before the dragons, there were cards.
item.description: Before there were dragons to steer, cities to build, or unicorns requiring an unreasonable amount of creative attention, there were cards.

item.title: The card table got a little out of hand.
item.description: A sensible studio might add another card game and call it a productive afternoon.

item.title: A U has entered the chat.
item.description: A brief developer detour into Canadian English, where “colour” brings an extra letter and “centre” rearranges the furniture.

item.title: Fewer buttons. More “one more go.”
item.description: The workbench has a recurring request: give the enjoyable part more room.

item.title: BooYang City: a town that grows with play
item.description: Animal friends, pastry inventions, go-karts, and new places to explore are taking shape in the development build.

item.title: GildenSpire: a dragon built to move
item.description: An original animated dragon, richer terrain, and a completed native campaign check move the world forward.

item.title: Small fixes that change the feel
item.description: Battle speed, sleep refreshes, saved progress, and creative tools received focused attention in the latest audit.

item.title: AI in the workshop—and in useful products
item.description: How AI-assisted development and carefully chosen product capabilities fit our old-school values.

item.title: Introducing GildenSpire: Flight or Fight
item.description: Raise a dragon, take direct control in the sky, and discover what happens when flying becomes fighting.

item.title: Why Flying Has to Be Fun
item.description: The journey should be gameplay: direct flight, enormous terrain, curiosity, and combat that rewards control.

item.title: Building Dragons That Actually Feel Different
item.description: GildenSpire dragons are being designed as different creatures—not one model wearing different colors.

item.title: From Search to Opportunity: Building Whomly
item.description: How a search-first interface can turn public professional research into useful context and a thoughtful next step.

item.title: Welcome to BooYang City
item.description: A connected city gives us room for a zoo, bakery, boutique, school, hospital, and almost anything fun that might open next.

item.title: Introducing Thumb Command: Save Planet Earth
item.description: Meet Blueguard and the worldwide arcade-defense campaign taking shape at Four of Hearts Interactive.

item.title: Making Sleep Data Feel Human
item.description: Sleep Readiness, Tonight’s Game Plan, Ask Amigo, Wind Down, and a small celestial companion give the numbers some warmth.

item.title: Building a Town That Refuses to Look Normal
item.description: Funky Town treats buildings as canvases and progression as a chance to make every neighborhood more expressive.

item.title: Building Unicorn Land Adventures
item.description: Unicorn creation, magical habitats, decorating, discovery, and mini-games define a distinct creative game.

item.title: Inside Princess Land Adventures
item.description: Character style, castle rooms, cooking, decorating, and mini-games begin forming one creative game.

item.title: People Lens Is Becoming Whomly
item.description: The working name is retiring. Whomly better fits the journey from discovery to context to possible opportunity.

item.title: HeartStack Unicorn Blast Joins the Workbench
item.description: A first look at colourful combos, crystal cages, boosters, and unicorn rescue.

item.title: Evil Doom Boy: Two Heroes, One Fight
item.description: Evil Doom Boy is one action-adventure game with Evil Doom Boy as the default hero and Evil Doom Girl as the alternate hero.

item.title: Bobby and the Breadstone
item.description: Bread-powered towers, branching paths, cheerful enemies, and one heroic dinosaur define Bobby’s direction.

item.title: Why We’re Building Sleep Amigo
item.description: The harder sleep problem is not collecting another number. It is understanding what may matter tonight.

item.title: The 4OH Card Table Adds Solitaire and War
item.description: Two familiar card games join Palace, Hearts, Spades, and Euchre in the Four of Hearts lineup.

item.title: Palace 0.1.9 Enters Founder Review
item.description: The flagship card-table build advances through hands-on founder testing.
